recommended_model.rationale: The order_items table serves as the central fact table as it contains transactional data related to each order, including product details and pricing. The dimension tables provide contextual information about customers, products, sellers, payment methods, and reviews, enabling comprehensive analysis of sales performance and customer behavior.

quality_findings: The geolocation table has 261831 duplicate rows, which may lead to inaccurate location-based analysis.
The order_reviews table has a high percentage of null values in review_comment_title (88.34%), indicating potential issues with customer feedback collection.
The order_reviews table also has a significant percentage of null values in review_comment_message (58.7%), which may limit qualitative insights from customer reviews.
data_science_opportunities: Churn prediction could be implemented by analyzing customer purchase patterns and review scores to identify at-risk customers.
Demand forecasting can be enhanced by utilizing historical sales data from order_items to predict future sales trends.
Customer segmentation analysis could be performed based on purchasing behavior and demographics to tailor marketing strategies.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(price) AS REAL) AS total_revenue FROM order_items;
kpis.why_it_matters: Total revenue is a key indicator of business performance, reflecting the overall sales generated.

kpis.name: Average Order Value
kpis.sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(price) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS average_order_value FROM order_items;
kpis.why_it_matters: Average order value helps assess customer spending behavior and can guide pricing strategies.

kpis.name: Revenue by Product Category
kpis.sql: SELECT p.product_category_name, CAST(SUM(oi.price) AS REAL) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_category_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 10;
kpis.why_it_matters: Understanding revenue by product category helps identify top-performing categories and informs inventory and marketing strategies.

kpis.name: Orders by Payment Type
kpis.sql: SELECT op.payment_type, COUNT(DISTINCT op.order_id) AS total_orders FROM order_payments op GROUP BY op.payment_type ORDER BY total_orders DESC LIMIT 10;
kpis.why_it_matters: Analyzing orders by payment type reveals customer preferences and can inform payment processing strategies.

kpis.name: Average Review Score
kpis.sql: SELECT CAST(AVG(review_score) AS REAL) AS average_review_score FROM order_reviews;
kpis.why_it_matters: Average review score is crucial for assessing customer satisfaction and product quality.

kpis.name: Top 10 Cities by Customer Count
kpis.sql: SELECT customer_city, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY customer_city ORDER BY customer_count DESC LIMIT 10;
kpis.why_it_matters: Identifying top cities by customer count helps target marketing efforts and optimize logistics.

insights: The total revenue for the period stands at R$13,591,643.70, indicating strong sales performance and overall business health.
The average order value is R$137.75, which suggests that customers are spending a reasonable amount per transaction; this insight can help in refining pricing strategies.
The top product category is 'health_beauty' with R$1,258,681.34 in revenue, highlighting a strong market demand that can guide inventory and marketing efforts.
Credit card payments dominate with 76,505 orders, showing a clear customer preference that can inform payment processing strategies.

The average review score is 4.09, reflecting a generally positive customer satisfaction level, although the high percentage of null values in review comments (88.34% for titles and 58.7% for messages) raises concerns about the quality of feedback collected, potentially limiting insights into customer experiences.
The top city for customer count is São Paulo with 15,540 customers, indicating a key market area that may benefit from targeted marketing and logistics optimization.
